heuristics: H1 (coverage; the load-bearing heuristic): the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z = s^d like uniform elements of the order-m subgroup H, so the success probability is 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39950 at K = 0.51. H2 and H2' (supply only): a fraction 1/2^20 of primes near q are H-primes (q^m = 1 mod r); gaps between consecutive H-primes are exponential with mean 2^20 ln q, so the L-th (L = 2^51.6503) H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^78 and a gap above 2^33 among the listed ones has probability < 2^-167 per list. Checked by the run's H-prime sanity block: 402 of the 6542 primes below 2^16 are sixteenth powers against 408.875 expected (binomial z = -0.34).

H3 (key bits): the 192-bit parity-selected y keys of the walked points behave like independent uniform strings across the six-element mu_6 orbits. This is a heuristic about coordinates of structured points; the end-to-end toy bins 16-bit truncated keys into 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads and reports occupancy chi^2 = 24.27 on 31 degrees of freedom (z = -0.85).

limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.
H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence).

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; the cluster model (no remote-memory instruction, 512-byte block transfers charged to sender and receiver, waiting nodes free) is the accepted lineage's definition restated here, and every shared price is re-derived in proof.md section 3 rather than inherited.
Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.490 bytes, claimed at its ceiling 2^122.5.

The per-record charge 160 is an itemised analytic count over a 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 128/122; it is not a hardware measurement.
